records.source: וַיְהִ֣י אַֽחֲרֵי־כֵ֗ן וַיִּשְׁאַל֩ דָּוִ֨ד בַּֽיהוָ֤ה׀לֵאמֹר֙ הַאֶעֱלֶ֗ה בְּאַחַת֙ עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֵלָ֖יו עֲלֵ֑ה וַיֹּ֧אמֶר דָּוִ֛ד אָ֥נָה אֶעֱלֶ֖ה וַיֹּ֥אמֶר חֶבְרֹֽנָה׃
records.gloss: And it was after thus, and asked David of Yahweh, saying, Shall I go up into one of [the] cities of Judah? And said Yahweh to him, Go up. And said David, Where shall I go up? And he said, To Hebron.
pieces: Some time after this, David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: "Shall I go up into any of the towns of Judah?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told him, "Go up." David asked, "Where should I go?" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered, "To Hebron."

L.1: And it was after this [that] David inquired of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Shall I go up into one of the cities of Judah?" And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to him, "Go up." And David said, "Where shall I go up?" And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "To Hebron."

R.1: After this, David asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Should I go up to one of the towns in Judah?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} told him, "Go." David asked, "Which town should I go to?" {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Hebron."

decisions.choice: inquired of the LORD: asked God for guidance, probably through the priest and the ephod
decisions.reason: David had asked the LORD in this way before, when the priest Abiathar brought him the ephod (1 Samuel 23:2, 4, 9-12; 30:7-8). The short yes-or-no question and the one-word answer fit that kind of asking.

decisions.choice: after this: after the news of Saul's death and David's lament for Saul and Jonathan
decisions.reason: The words join this chapter to chapter 1. With Saul dead, David now asks where he should go.

decisions.choice: Hebron: an old city in the hill country of Judah
decisions.reason: Hebron was where Abraham bought a burial place for his family (Genesis 23:2, 19), and it had been given to Caleb of Judah (Joshua 14:13-14). David had sent gifts to its leaders (1 Samuel 30:31). It stands high in the hills, so from the south one "goes up" to it.

decisions.choice: towns
decisions.reason: The word is usually "city", but the places of Judah were small walled settlements, so Balanced and Readable say "towns".

decisions.choice: The LORD answered
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he said". Readable names the speaker so a young reader does not lose track.

records.heading: David is anointed king over Judah

records.source: וַיַּ֤עַל שָׁם֙ דָּוִ֔ד וְגַ֖ם שְׁתֵּ֣י נָשָׁ֑יו אֲחִינֹ֨עַם֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵלִ֔ית וַאֲבִיגַ֕יִל אֵ֖שֶׁת נָבָ֥ל הַֽכַּרְמְלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And went up there David, and also [the] two of his wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail [the] wife of Nabal the Carmelite.
pieces: So David went up there, and his two wives went with him: Ahinoam of Jezreel, and Abigail, who had been the wife of Nabal of Carmel.

L.2: So David went up there, and also his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelite and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.

R.2: So David went to Hebron. His two wives went with him. One was Ahinoam from Jezreel. The other was Abigail, whose husband Nabal from Carmel had died.

decisions.choice: Ahinoam and Abigail: the two wives David had married while he was in hiding
decisions.reason: David married both women after Nabal's death (1 Samuel 25:39-43), and they had lived with him among the Philistines and at Ziklag (1 Samuel 27:3; 30:5, 18).

decisions.choice: Jezreel and Carmel: towns in the hills of Judah
decisions.reason: This Jezreel is a town of Judah (Joshua 15:56), not the northern valley named in verse 9. Carmel is a town south of Hebron (Joshua 15:55; 1 Samuel 25:2), not Mount Carmel on the coast.

decisions.choice: wife of Nabal: Nabal's widow
decisions.reason: Nabal had died (1 Samuel 25:37-38). She is still named by her first husband, as people were then known by their family ties.

decisions.choice: who had been the wife of (Balanced); whose husband ... had died (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The wife of Nabal" could make a reader think Nabal was still alive. Balanced and Readable say what the phrase means here.

decisions.choice: to Hebron
decisions.reason: Readable names the place "there" points to (verse 1).

records.source: וַאֲנָשָׁ֧יו אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֛וֹ הֶעֱלָ֥ה דָוִ֖ד אִ֣ישׁ וּבֵית֑וֹ וַיֵּשְׁב֖וּ בְּעָרֵ֥י חֶבְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And his men who [were] with him brought up David, each and his household, and they dwelt in [the] cities of Hebron.
pieces: David also brought up his men, every one of them with his household, and they made their homes in the towns around Hebron.

L.3: And his men who [were] with him David brought up, each man and his household, and they lived in the cities of Hebron.

R.3: David also took along the men who had been with him, and each man brought his family. They made their homes in the towns near Hebron.

decisions.choice: his men: the band that had followed David while Saul hunted him
decisions.reason: About six hundred men had gathered to David, and they had lived with their families at Ziklag (1 Samuel 22:2; 27:2-3; 30:3).

decisions.choice: cities of Hebron: the towns and villages that belonged to Hebron
decisions.reason: Hebron itself could not hold so many families. The phrase means the settlements in its district, as towns are said to have their "villages" (Joshua 15:54).

decisions.choice: household: a man's wife, children and others who lived under his care
decisions.reason: The word "house" covers everyone in a man's family home, not only the building.

decisions.choice: the towns around Hebron; the towns near Hebron
decisions.reason: "Cities of Hebron" would suggest Hebron was several cities. Balanced and Readable say how the towns were related to it.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּמְשְׁחוּ־שָׁ֧ם אֶת־דָּוִ֛ד לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֤דוּ לְדָוִד֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר אַנְשֵׁי֙ יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֔ד אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָבְר֖וּ אֶת־שָׁאֽוּל׃ס
records.gloss: And came [the] men of Judah and anointed there David as king over [the] house of Judah. And they told David, saying, [The] men of Jabesh-gilead [are those] who buried Saul.
pieces: Then the men of Judah came and anointed David there as king over the house of Judah. David was told, "The men of Jabesh-gilead were the ones who buried Saul."

L.4: And the men of Judah came, and they anointed David there as king over the house of Judah. And they told David, saying, "[It was] the men of Jabesh-gilead who buried Saul."

R.4: The men of Judah came to Hebron. There they poured oil on David's head and made him king over the people of Judah. Someone told David, "The men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul."

decisions.choice: anointed David as king: poured oil on him to set him apart as king
decisions.reason: Samuel had anointed David privately years before (1 Samuel 16:13). Now his own tribe anoints him in public. All Israel will anoint him later (5:3).

decisions.choice: the house of Judah: the tribe of Judah as one people
decisions.reason: "House" here means a family line grown into a tribe. David's kingdom at this point is Judah alone (verse 10).

decisions.choice: the men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul
decisions.reason: After the Philistines hung the bodies of Saul and his sons on the wall of Beth-shan, the men of Jabesh-gilead took them down by night and buried them (1 Samuel 31:11-13). Saul had once saved their town (1 Samuel 11:1-11).

decisions.choice: they told David: someone brought David word
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it simply means David was told.

decisions.choice: David was told (Balanced); Someone told David (Readable)
decisions.reason: English needs either a passive or an unnamed "someone" for the Hebrew's unnamed "they". Readable also says "the people of Judah" for "the house of Judah".

decisions.choice: poured oil on David's head and made him king
decisions.reason: Readable explains what anointing was (see m1), as in Psalm 133:2 and 1 Samuel 10:1, where oil is poured on the head.

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מַלְאָכִ֔ים אֶל־אַנְשֵׁ֖י יָבֵ֣ישׁ גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֗ם בְּרֻכִ֤ים אַתֶּם֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֜ם הַחֶ֣סֶד הַזֶּ֗ה עִם־אֲדֹֽנֵיכֶם֙ עִם־שָׁא֔וּל וַֽתִּקְבְּר֖וּ אֹתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And sent David messengers to [the] men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, Blessed [are] you to Yahweh, who did this steadfast love with your lord, with Saul, and buried him.
pieces: David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead to say to them, "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you, because you showed this faithful love to your lord Saul by burying him.

L.5: And David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead and said to them, "Blessed [are] you by {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, you who have done this steadfast love with your lord, with Saul, and have buried him.

R.5: David sent messengers to the men of Jabesh-gilead with this message: "May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} bless you! You showed faithful love to Saul, your master, when you buried him.

decisions.choice: blessed are you by the LORD: may the LORD bless you
decisions.reason: This is a set form of blessing, a wish that the LORD will do good to someone (Ruth 2:20; 3:10; 1 Samuel 23:21).

decisions.choice: steadfast love: loyalty kept to someone one is bound to
decisions.reason: The word names faithful kindness within a bond, here the bond of subjects to their king. They kept faith with Saul even after his death, as Ruth had with the dead of her family (Ruth 1:8).

decisions.choice: and buried him: the burial was the act of loyalty
decisions.reason: The last clause explains what "this steadfast love" was.

decisions.choice: faithful love
decisions.reason: As set for these books, Literal "steadfast love" and Balanced and Readable "faithful love" (Exodus 34:6). Readable says "master" for "lord" so it is not mistaken for God.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֕ה יַֽעַשׂ־יְהוָ֥ה עִמָּכֶ֖ם חֶ֣סֶד וֶאֱמֶ֑ת וְגַ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י אֶעֱשֶׂ֤ה אִתְּכֶם֙ הַטּוֹבָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲשִׂיתֶ֖ם הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And now may do Yahweh with you steadfast love and faithfulness; and also I will do with you this good, because you did this thing.
pieces: Now may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} show you faithful love and truth. I too will treat you well, because you have done this.

L.6: And now may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} do steadfast love and faithfulness with you. And I also will do with you this good, because you have done this thing.

R.6: Now may {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} show you {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love and be faithful to you. I will also be good to you because of what you did.

decisions.choice: steadfast love and faithfulness: loyal kindness that can be relied on
decisions.reason: The two words often go together for the LORD's faithful care (Exodus 34:6; Genesis 24:27). David asks the LORD to repay them in kind for the loyalty they showed.

decisions.choice: this good: the good David himself will now do for them
alternatives: I will repay you for this good deed
decisions.reason: "This good" could point back to their deed, but the verb "I will do" makes it David's own promised kindness, matching what they did for Saul.

decisions.choice: I also: David as the new king promises his favor
decisions.reason: The promise prepares for verse 7, where David tells them he is now king of Judah.

decisions.choice: show you his faithful love and be faithful to you
decisions.reason: Readable turns the pair of nouns into two plain phrases, and supplies "his".

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀תֶּחֱזַ֣קְנָה יְדֵיכֶ֗ם וִֽהְיוּ֙ לִבְנֵי־חַ֔יִל כִּי־מֵ֖ת אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֣ם שָׁא֑וּל וְגַם־אֹתִ֗י מָשְׁח֧וּ בֵית־יְהוּדָ֛ה לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עֲלֵיהֶֽם׃פ
records.gloss: And now let be strong your hands and be sons of valor, for has died your lord Saul, and also me have anointed [the] house of Judah as king over them.
pieces: So now be strong and brave, for Saul your lord is dead, and the house of Judah has anointed me king over them."

L.7: And now let your hands be strong, and be sons of valor, for your lord Saul is dead, and the house of Judah has also anointed me as king over them."

R.7: Now be strong and brave. Saul your master is dead, and the people of Judah have anointed me to be their king."

decisions.choice: let your hands be strong: take courage
decisions.reason: Strong hands stand for courage and resolve (Judges 7:11; 2 Samuel 16:21).

decisions.choice: sons of valor: brave and able men
decisions.reason: "Son of" a quality means a person marked by it.

decisions.choice: an unspoken invitation to accept David as king
decisions.reason: By setting Saul's death beside his own anointing, David suggests that the men of Jabesh-gilead should now look to him. He does not say it outright, and the translation leaves it unstated too.

decisions.choice: be strong and brave
decisions.reason: The two pictures are folded into one plain call to courage.

records.source: וְאַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־נֵ֔ר שַׂר־צָבָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְשָׁא֑וּל לָקַ֗ח אֶת־אִ֥ישׁ בֹּ֨שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֖הוּ מַחֲנָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And Abner son of Ner, commander of [the] army that [was] to Saul, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over [to] Mahanaim.
pieces: Meanwhile Abner son of Ner, the commander of Saul's army, had taken Saul's son Ish-bosheth and brought him across to Mahanaim.

L.8: And Abner son of Ner, commander of the army that [belonged] to Saul, had taken Ish-bosheth son of Saul and brought him over [to] Mahanaim.

R.8: Abner, the son of Ner, had been the army commander for Saul. He had taken Saul's son Ish-bosheth across the Jordan River to the town of Mahanaim.

decisions.choice: Ish-bosheth: "man of shame", standing in Samuel for his name Eshbaal
decisions.reason: In 1 Chronicles 8:33 and 9:39 this son of Saul is called Eshbaal, "man of Baal" or "Baal exists". "Baal" means "lord" or "master" and could once be used of Israel's God, but it was also the name of the Canaanite god, so in Samuel the word "bosheth", "shame", stands in its place. The same change gives Mephibosheth (4:4) for Merib-baal (1 Chronicles 8:34) and Jerubbesheth (11:21) for Jerubbaal (Judges 6:32), and "the shame" stands for Baal in Jeremiah 3:24 and Hosea 9:10. The name is kept as the text of Samuel has it.

decisions.choice: had taken: told as background, at about the same time as David's anointing
decisions.reason: The sentence begins with Abner rather than with a verb, a Hebrew way of turning to another scene that runs alongside the first.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: a town in Gilead, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jacob named the place (Genesis 32:3), and it lay in the land of Gad (Joshua 13:26). It was far from the Philistines, who had taken towns west of the Jordan after Saul's defeat (1 Samuel 31:7). "Brought him over" means across the river.

decisions.choice: Abner: Saul's cousin and the commander of his army
decisions.reason: Abner's father Ner was Saul's uncle (1 Samuel 14:50-51). Now he, not the LORD or a prophet, is the one who makes Saul's son king.

decisions.choice: across the Jordan River to the town of Mahanaim
decisions.reason: Readable names the river the verb implies and says Mahanaim is a town. "Commander of the army" follows the wording set for these books (Readable "army commander").

records.heading: Ish-bosheth becomes king over Israel

records.source: וַיַּמְלִכֵ֨הוּ֙ אֶל־הַגִּלְעָ֔ד וְאֶל־הָאֲשׁוּרִ֖י וְאֶֽל־יִזְרְעֶ֑אל וְעַל־אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ וְעַל־בִּנְיָמִ֔ן וְעַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כֻּלֹּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: And he made him king to the Gilead and to the Ashurite and to Jezreel and over Ephraim and over Benjamin and over Israel, all of it.
pieces: He made him king over Gilead, the Ashurites and Jezreel, over Ephraim and Benjamin, and over all Israel.

L.9: And he made him king for Gilead and for the Ashurites and for Jezreel, and over Ephraim and over Benjamin and over Israel, all of it.

R.9: Abner made Ish-bosheth king of Gilead, of the Ashurites and of Jezreel, and of Ephraim and Benjamin. He became king over all Israel.

decisions.choice: the Ashurites: a people not otherwise known; perhaps the tribe of Asher
decisions.reason: The name does not mean Assyria. A people in the north between Gilead and Jezreel is expected, and the tribe of Asher fits, as one early Aramaic translation reads. Some other early translations (Syriac and Latin) read "Geshurites", but Geshur had its own king (3:3), so that is less likely. The Hebrew form is kept; reviewers should check the ancient versions.

decisions.choice: Jezreel: here the broad valley in the north
decisions.reason: This is the great valley between Galilee and the hills of Ephraim (Joshua 17:16), not the town of Judah in verse 2.

decisions.choice: and over Israel, all of it: a summary of the whole kingdom apart from Judah
decisions.reason: After naming regions and tribes, the list sums them up as all Israel. The list changes its preposition partway through, from one meaning "to" or "for" to one meaning "over", but this does not seem to change the sense.

decisions.choice: Abner made Ish-bosheth king ... He became king over all Israel.
decisions.reason: Readable names both men and makes the summary its own sentence.

records.source: בֶּן־אַרְבָּעִ֨ים שָׁנָ֜ה אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֣שֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁא֗וּל בְּמָלְכוֹ֙ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּשְׁתַּ֥יִם שָׁנִ֖ים מָלָ֑ךְ אַ֚ךְ בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֔ה הָי֖וּ אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: A son of forty years [was] Ish-bosheth son of Saul when he became king over Israel, and two years he reigned. Only [the] house of Judah were after David.
pieces: Ish-bosheth son of Saul was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah followed David.

L.10: Ish-bosheth son of Saul [was] a son of forty years when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years. Only the house of Judah were after David.

R.10: Ish-bosheth was forty years old when he became king over Israel, and he ruled for two years. But the people of Judah were loyal to David.

decisions.choice: a son of forty years: forty years old
decisions.reason: This is the usual Hebrew way of giving a person's age.

decisions.choice: two years: shorter than David's seven and a half years in Hebron (verse 11)
decisions.reason: The text does not explain the difference. Ish-bosheth may have been made king some years after Saul's death, once Abner had won back the land from the Philistines, or the two years may count only part of the time before David became king of all Israel (5:1-5).

decisions.choice: were after David: followed David as their king
decisions.reason: To be "after" someone is to follow them as leader (1 Kings 12:20).

decisions.choice: was ... when he became king over Israel, and he reigned two years
decisions.reason: This is the wording set for the regnal formula in these books. Readable says "ruled" and "were loyal to".

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִסְפַּ֣ר הַיָּמִ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה דָוִ֥ד מֶ֛לֶךְ בְּחֶבְר֖וֹן עַל־בֵּ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִ֖ים וְשִׁשָּׁ֥ה חֳדָשִֽׁים׃ס
records.gloss: And was the number of the days that was David king in Hebron over [the] house of Judah seven years and six months.
pieces: David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah for seven years and six months.

L.11: And the number of the days that David was king in Hebron over the house of Judah was seven years and six months.

R.11: David ruled over Judah from Hebron for seven and a half years.

decisions.choice: the number of the days: the length of time
decisions.reason: "Days" here means a span of time.

decisions.choice: seven years and six months: repeated when David's reign is summed up
decisions.reason: The same length is given in 5:5 and 1 Chronicles 3:4; 1 Kings 2:11 rounds it to seven years.

decisions.choice: seven and a half years
decisions.reason: Readable uses the simpler phrase for the same length of time.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ אַבְנֵ֣ר בֶּן־נֵ֔ר וְעַבְדֵ֖י אִֽישׁ־בֹּ֣שֶׁת בֶּן־שָׁא֑וּל מִֽמַּחֲנַ֖יִם גִּבְעֽוֹנָה׃
records.gloss: And went out Abner son of Ner and [the] servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul from Mahanaim to Gibeon.
pieces: Abner son of Ner set out from Mahanaim for Gibeon with the men of Ish-bosheth son of Saul.

L.12: And Abner son of Ner went out, and the servants of Ish-bosheth son of Saul, from Mahanaim to Gibeon.

R.12: Abner, the son of Ner, marched from Mahanaim to Gibeon with the soldiers of Saul's son Ish-bosheth.

decisions.choice: went out: marched out to battle
decisions.reason: "Go out" is often said of an army taking the field (1 Samuel 8:20; 18:30).

decisions.choice: Gibeon: a town of Benjamin near the border of Judah
decisions.reason: Gibeon lay a few miles northwest of Jerusalem (Joshua 9:3; 18:25). Abner leads his army back across the Jordan toward David's territory.

decisions.choice: the servants of Ish-bosheth: the king's fighting men
decisions.reason: A king's "servants" can be his officials or, as here and in verses 13, 15, 17 and 30-31, his soldiers.

decisions.choice: men (Balanced); soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Here the king's "servants" are his fighting men, so Balanced says "men" and Readable "soldiers"; Literal keeps "servants".

records.heading: The battle at Gibeon

records.source: וְיוֹאָ֨ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֜ה וְעַבְדֵ֤י דָוִד֙ יָֽצְא֔וּ וַֽיִּפְגְּשׁ֛וּם עַל־בְּרֵכַ֥ת גִּבְע֖וֹן יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיֵּ֨שְׁב֜וּ אֵ֤לֶּה עַל־הַבְּרֵכָה֙ מִזֶּ֔ה וְאֵ֥לֶּה עַל־הַבְּרֵכָ֖ה מִזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And Joab son of Zeruiah and [the] servants of David went out, and they met them by [the] pool of Gibeon together; and they sat, these by the pool on this [side] and these by the pool on this [side].
pieces: Joab son of Zeruiah and David's men also went out, and the two forces met at the pool of Gibeon. They sat down across the pool from each other, one group on each side.

L.13: And Joab son of Zeruiah and the servants of David went out, and they met them together at the pool of Gibeon. And they sat down, these at the pool on this [side] and those at the pool on that [side].

R.13: Joab, the son of Zeruiah, also marched out with David's soldiers. The two armies met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner's men sat down on one side of the pool, and Joab's men faced them from the other side.

decisions.choice: Joab son of Zeruiah: David's nephew
decisions.reason: Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16), and her three sons are named after her (verse 18). Joab already led David's men.

decisions.choice: the pool of Gibeon: a large water source at Gibeon
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 41:12 also speaks of "the great waters" at Gibeon. It was a natural meeting place for two forces.

decisions.choice: together: the two sides came to the same place
decisions.reason: The word says that they met each other there, not that they arrived at the same moment.

decisions.choice: David's men (Balanced); David's soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

decisions.choice: Abner's men ... Joab's men
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "these ... and these". Readable names the two groups; the text does not say which side each sat on, and the choice here changes nothing.

records.source: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַבְנֵר֙ אֶל־יוֹאָ֔ב יָק֤וּמוּ נָא֙ הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וִֽישַׂחֲק֖וּ לְפָנֵ֑ינוּ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יוֹאָ֖ב יָקֻֽמוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Abner to Joab, Let arise please the young men and let them play before us. And said Joab, Let them arise.
pieces: Then Abner said to Joab, "Let some of the young men get up and hold a contest in front of us." Joab answered, "Let them get up."

L.14: And Abner said to Joab, "Let the young men arise, please, and let them play before us." And Joab said, "Let them arise."

R.14: Abner said to Joab, "Let some of our young soldiers fight each other while we watch." Joab said, "All right, let them."

decisions.choice: play: hold a contest of arms, staged like a sport
decisions.reason: The verb means play, sport or entertain (Judges 16:25). Here it names combat between chosen fighters before the two leaders. Whether it was meant as a show of skill or as a fight between champions to settle the matter, as Goliath proposed (1 Samuel 17:8-9), is not said; it ends in death either way (verse 16).

decisions.choice: young men: young fighting men
decisions.reason: The word for young men is often used for soldiers (1 Samuel 21:3; 25:5).

decisions.choice: please: a polite word that softens the proposal
decisions.reason: Abner frames the deadly contest as a courteous suggestion.

decisions.choice: hold a contest (Balanced); fight each other while we watch (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Play" alone would hide that this was armed combat. Balanced keeps the sense of a staged event; Readable says plainly what happened. Both drop the softening "please".

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֖מוּ וַיַּעַבְר֣וּ בְמִסְפָּ֑ר שְׁנֵ֧ים עָשָׂ֣ר לְבִנְיָמִ֗ן וּלְאִ֥ישׁ בֹּ֨שֶׁת֙ בֶּן־שָׁא֔וּל וּשְׁנֵ֥ים עָשָׂ֖ר מֵעַבְדֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And they arose and passed over by number, twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of [the] servants of David.
pieces: So they got up and went forward one by one as they were counted: twelve for Benjamin and Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of David's men.

L.15: And they arose and passed over by number: twelve for Benjamin and for Ish-bosheth son of Saul, and twelve of the servants of David.

R.15: So twelve men from Benjamin stepped forward to fight for Ish-bosheth, Saul's son, and twelve of David's soldiers stepped forward too. They were counted as they came.

decisions.choice: passed over by number: went forward one by one and were counted
decisions.reason: "Passing by" and being counted is used of a flock passing under the shepherd's hand (Jeremiah 33:13). Each side matched the other man for man.

decisions.choice: for Benjamin: Saul's own tribe, the heart of Ish-bosheth's support
decisions.reason: Saul was from Benjamin (1 Samuel 9:1-2), and the Benjaminites rally to Abner in verse 25.

decisions.choice: stepped forward ... They were counted as they came.
decisions.reason: Readable gives the counting its own sentence and says "David's soldiers" as in verse 12.

records.source: וַֽיַּחֲזִ֜קוּ אִ֣ישׁ׀בְּרֹ֣אשׁ רֵעֵ֗הוּ וְחַרְבּוֹ֙ בְּצַ֣ד רֵעֵ֔הוּ וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ יַחְדָּ֑ו וַיִּקְרָא֙ לַמָּק֣וֹם הַה֔וּא חֶלְקַ֥ת הַצֻּרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And they seized each by [the] head of his fellow, and his sword in [the] side of his fellow, and they fell together. And one called that place Helkath-hazzurim, which [is] in Gibeon.
pieces: Each man caught his opponent by the head and thrust his sword into his side, and they fell down together. So that place in Gibeon was named Helkath-hazzurim.

L.16: And they seized each one his fellow by the head, and his sword [was] in his fellow's side, and they fell together. And one called that place Helkath-hazzurim, which [is] in Gibeon.

R.16: Each man grabbed the man in front of him by the head and stabbed him in the side with his sword, and they all fell dead together. So that place in Gibeon was named Helkath-hazzurim, which means Field of Sharp Edges.

decisions.choice: Helkath-hazzurim: "field of sharp edges", either flint knives or sword blades
decisions.reason: "Helkath" means a plot of land. "Hazzurim" is the plural of a word for rock or flint, which is also used for the edge of a sword (Psalm 89:44), so the name may mean "Field of Flints" or "Field of Blades"; both point to the killing that gave it its name. The early Greek translation has a different name, "Field of the Plotters", from a Hebrew word that looks almost the same. Another suggestion links it with "side" earlier in the verse. The name is kept as written.

decisions.choice: his sword in his fellow's side: each struck the other at the same moment
decisions.reason: The clause has no verb, a quick picture of all the thrusts at once. All twenty-four fall together, so the contest settles nothing and the full battle follows (verse 17).

decisions.choice: one called: the place came to be called
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject; it means people gave the place this name.

decisions.choice: which means Field of Sharp Edges
decisions.reason: Readable gives the meaning of the name. "Sharp edges" is chosen because it fits both flint and sword blades (see m1).

decisions.choice: was named
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a passive for the Hebrew's unnamed "one".

records.source: וַתְּהִ֧י הַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה קָשָׁ֥ה עַד־מְאֹ֖ד בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וַיִּנָּ֤גֶף אַבְנֵר֙ וְאַנְשֵׁ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִפְנֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י דָוִֽד׃
records.gloss: And was the battle severe up to muchness on the day the that, and was defeated Abner and [the] men of Israel before [the] servants of David.
pieces: A very hard battle followed that day, and David's men defeated Abner and the men of Israel.

L.17: And the battle was very severe on that day, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated before the servants of David.

R.17: Then a fierce battle broke out that day. David's soldiers beat Abner and the men of Israel.

decisions.choice: the battle: the contest turned into a full battle
decisions.reason: The deaths of all twenty-four champions (verse 16) brought both armies into the fight.

decisions.choice: the men of Israel: the forces of the northern tribes under Ish-bosheth
decisions.reason: In this chapter "Israel" is the kingdom of Ish-bosheth, set against Judah (verses 9-10).

decisions.choice: David's men defeated Abner
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn "was defeated before" into an active sentence with the same meaning.

records.source: וַיִּֽהְיוּ־שָׁ֗ם שְׁלֹשָׁה֙ בְּנֵ֣י צְרוּיָ֔ה יוֹאָ֥ב וַאֲבִישַׁ֖י וַעֲשָׂהאֵ֑ל וַעֲשָׂהאֵל֙ קַ֣ל בְּרַגְלָ֔יו כְּאַחַ֥ד הַצְּבָיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And were there three sons of Zeruiah: Joab and Abishai and Asahel. And Asahel [was] light in his feet like one of the gazelles that [are] in the field.
pieces: The three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab, Abishai and Asahel. Asahel was as quick on his feet as a wild gazelle.

L.18: And the three sons of Zeruiah were there: Joab and Abishai and Asahel. And Asahel [was] light on his feet like one of the gazelles that [are] in the field.

R.18: All three of Zeruiah's sons were in the battle: Joab, Abishai and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a gazelle in the open country.

decisions.choice: Joab, Abishai and Asahel: David's nephews
decisions.reason: All three are named in 1 Chronicles 2:16. Abishai had gone with David into Saul's camp (1 Samuel 26:6), and Asahel is later listed among David's mighty men (23:24).

decisions.choice: light on his feet like a gazelle: a very fast runner
decisions.reason: Swiftness like a gazelle or deer is praise for a warrior (22:34; 1 Chronicles 12:9). The speed that makes Asahel famous leads to his death.

decisions.choice: in the field: in the wild, open country
decisions.reason: The gazelle is a wild animal of the open land, not a tame one.

decisions.choice: as quick on his feet as a wild gazelle
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "light on his feet" into a common English phrase for speed and "in the field" into "wild".

records.source: וַיִּרְדֹּ֥ף עֲשָׂהאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְלֹֽא־נָטָ֣ה לָלֶ֗כֶת עַל־הַיָּמִין֙ וְעַֽל־הַשְּׂמֹ֔אול מֵאַחֲרֵ֖י אַבְנֵֽר׃
records.gloss: And pursued Asahel after Abner, and not he turned to go to the right or to the left from after Abner.
pieces: Asahel went after Abner and kept on his track without turning aside to the right or the left.

L.19: And Asahel pursued after Abner, and he did not turn to go to the right or to the left from following Abner.

R.19: Asahel chased Abner. He ran straight after him and did not turn aside at all.

decisions.choice: did not turn to the right or to the left: kept his whole aim on Abner
decisions.reason: Not turning aside describes a fixed purpose. Asahel ignores every other fighter and goes after the enemy commander alone.

decisions.choice: did not turn aside at all
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sense of the idiom without the pair "right ... left".

records.source: וַיִּ֤פֶן אַבְנֵר֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הַאַתָּ֥ה זֶ֖ה עֲשָׂהאֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אָנֹֽכִי׃
records.gloss: And turned Abner behind him and said, [Is] you this Asahel? And he said, I.
pieces: Abner looked back and called out, "Is that you, Asahel?" "It is," he answered.

L.20: And Abner turned behind him and said, "Is this you, Asahel?" And he said, "[It is] I."

R.20: Abner looked back and said, "Is that you, Asahel?" "Yes, it is," Asahel answered.

decisions.choice: is this you: "is it really you?"
decisions.reason: The small word "this" adds force to the question. Abner recognizes the young man and knows whose brother he is (verse 22).

decisions.choice: Asahel answered
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר ל֣וֹ אַבְנֵ֗ר נְטֵ֤ה לְךָ֙ עַל־יְמִֽינְךָ֙ א֣וֹ עַל־שְׂמֹאלֶ֔ךָ וֶאֱחֹ֣ז לְךָ֗ אֶחָד֙ מֵֽהַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְקַח־לְךָ֖ אֶת־חֲלִצָת֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־אָבָ֣ה עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל לָס֖וּר מֵאַחֲרָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said to him Abner, Turn for yourself to your right or to your left, and seize for yourself one of the young men, and take for yourself his spoil. And not was willing Asahel to turn aside from after him.
pieces: Abner said to him, "Turn off to your right or your left. Catch one of the young men and strip him of his gear for yourself." But Asahel would not stop following him.

L.21: And Abner said to him, "Turn aside to your right or to your left, and seize for yourself one of the young men, and take for yourself his spoil." But Asahel was not willing to turn aside from following him.

R.21: Abner said to him, "Turn away to the right or the left. Go after one of the younger soldiers and take his weapons as your prize." But Asahel would not stop chasing him.

decisions.choice: spoil: the armor and weapons stripped from a fallen fighter
decisions.reason: The word is used again only in Judges 14:19, of the clothing Samson stripped from the men he killed. A warrior's trophy was the gear of the man he had beaten.

decisions.choice: Abner urges Asahel to win his trophy from a lesser fighter
decisions.reason: Abner is telling Asahel to pick an opponent his own size. As verse 22 makes clear, he does not want to kill him.

decisions.choice: for yourself: for your own good
decisions.reason: The repeated "for yourself" presses the advice on Asahel; it is in his own interest to turn aside.

decisions.choice: strip him of his gear (Balanced); take his weapons as your prize (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Spoil" today suggests food going bad. Balanced and Readable say what was taken.

records.source: וַיֹּ֧סֶף ע֣וֹד אַבְנֵ֗ר לֵאמֹר֙ אֶל־עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל ס֥וּר לְךָ֖ מֵאַֽחֲרָ֑י לָ֤מָּה אַכֶּ֨כָּה֙ אַ֔רְצָה וְאֵיךְ֙ אֶשָּׂ֣א פָנַ֔י אֶל־יוֹאָ֖ב אָחִֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And again repeated Abner to say to Asahel, Turn aside for yourself from after me. Why shall I strike you to [the] ground? And how shall I lift my face to Joab your brother?
pieces: Abner warned Asahel once more, "Stop chasing me! Why should I have to strike you down? How could I look your brother Joab in the face?"

L.22: And Abner again said to Asahel, "Turn aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the ground? And how would I lift my face to Joab your brother?"

R.22: Abner warned Asahel again, "Stop following me! I do not want to kill you. How could I ever face your brother Joab after that?"

decisions.choice: strike you to the ground: kill you
decisions.reason: Abner is sure he can kill Asahel and does not want to.

decisions.choice: lift my face to: look someone in the eye without shame
decisions.reason: To lift the face is to meet another person openly, with nothing to hide (Job 11:15).

decisions.choice: Joab your brother: killing Asahel would make Joab his deadly enemy
decisions.reason: A close relative was expected to avenge a killing. Joab later kills Abner for Asahel's death (3:27, 30).

decisions.choice: I do not want to kill you.
decisions.reason: Readable turns Abner's question "Why should I strike you to the ground?" into the statement it implies.

records.source: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן לָס֗וּר וַיַּכֵּ֣הוּ אַבְנֵר֩ בְּאַחֲרֵ֨י הַחֲנִ֜ית אֶל־הַחֹ֗מֶשׁ וַתֵּצֵ֤א הַֽחֲנִית֙ מֵאַחֲרָ֔יו וַיִּפָּל־שָׁ֖ם וַיָּ֣מָת תַּחְתָּ֑יו וַיְהִ֡י כָּל־הַבָּ֣א אֶֽל־הַמָּקוֹם֩ אֲשֶׁר־נָ֨פַל שָׁ֧ם עֲשָׂהאֵ֛ל וַיָּמֹ֖ת וַֽיַּעֲמֹֽדוּ׃
records.gloss: And he refused to turn aside, and struck him Abner with [the] back end of the spear into the belly, and went out the spear from behind him, and he fell there and died in his place. And it was, all the [one] coming to the place where fell there Asahel and died, and they stood still.
pieces: But Asahel refused to turn away. So Abner struck him in the belly with the butt of his spear, and the spear came out through his back. He fell there and died on the spot. Everyone who came to the place where Asahel had fallen and died stopped and stood still.

L.23: But he refused to turn aside, and Abner struck him with the back end of the spear in the belly, and the spear came out from behind him; and he fell there and died in his place. And it was [that] all who came to the place where Asahel fell there and died stood still.

R.23: But Asahel would not turn away. So Abner stabbed him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. It went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died right there. Everyone who came to the place where Asahel's body lay stopped and stood still.

decisions.choice: the back end of the spear: the butt, which could be pointed
decisions.reason: A spear's butt often had a metal point so it could be stuck in the ground (1 Samuel 26:7). Abner seems to have thrust it backward at Asahel, who was close behind him and running hard, so the blow went right through him.

decisions.choice: the belly: the stomach
decisions.reason: The same word is used for the place of the fatal blow in 3:27, 4:6 and 20:10. An older reading took it as "the fifth rib", but "belly" is the sense.

decisions.choice: in his place: on the spot
decisions.reason: He died where he fell.

decisions.choice: all who came stood still: each man halted when he reached the body
decisions.reason: The sentence pictures men coming one after another to the place and stopping at the sight of Asahel lying dead. Verse 24 tells of the two brothers who did not stop.

decisions.choice: where Asahel's body lay
decisions.reason: Readable describes the place by what the men saw there.

records.source: וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֛וּ יוֹאָ֥ב וַאֲבִישַׁ֖י אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֑ר וְהַשֶּׁ֣מֶשׁ בָּ֔אָה וְהֵ֗מָּה בָּ֚אוּ עַד־גִּבְעַ֣ת אַמָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־פְּנֵי־גִ֔יחַ דֶּ֖רֶךְ מִדְבַּ֥ר גִּבְעֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And pursued Joab and Abishai after Abner. And the sun went in, and they came to [the] hill of Ammah, which [is] on [the] face of Giah, [the] way of [the] wilderness of Gibeon.
pieces: But Joab and Abishai kept up the chase after Abner. As the sun was setting, they reached the hill of Ammah, which faces Giah on the road to the wilderness of Gibeon.

L.24: And Joab and Abishai pursued after Abner. And the sun was going down when they came to the hill of Ammah, which [is] before Giah, [on the] way [to] the wilderness of Gibeon.

R.24: But Joab and Abishai kept chasing Abner. The sun was going down when they reached the hill of Ammah. It is across from Giah, beside the road that leads into the dry, open country near Gibeon.

decisions.choice: Ammah and Giah: places not known from anywhere else
decisions.reason: Neither name appears again in the Bible. The road toward the wilderness suggests they lay east of Gibeon, on the way down to the Jordan valley where Abner was heading (verse 29).

decisions.choice: the sun was going down: the time when they arrived
decisions.reason: The clause sets the scene: the chase had lasted the whole day.

decisions.choice: wilderness: open, dry grazing land
decisions.reason: The word means land too dry to farm, used for grazing flocks, not sandy desert.

decisions.choice: the dry, open country
decisions.reason: Readable explains "wilderness" in plain words.

records.source: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ בְנֵֽי־בִנְיָמִן֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּהְי֖וּ לַאֲגֻדָּ֣ה אֶחָ֑ת וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ עַ֥ל רֹאשׁ־גִּבְעָ֖ה אֶחָֽת׃
records.gloss: And gathered themselves [the] sons of Benjamin after Abner, and they became one band, and they stood on [the] top of one hill.
pieces: The Benjaminites rallied around Abner and formed a single unit, and they held their ground on a hilltop.

L.25: And the sons of Benjamin gathered themselves behind Abner, and they became one band, and they stood on the top of one hill.

R.25: The men from the tribe of Benjamin came together behind Abner. They formed one group and stood ready on top of a hill.

decisions.choice: gathered behind Abner: rallied to him as their leader
decisions.reason: "Behind" someone is following his lead. Saul's own tribe stays with Saul's commander (verse 15).

decisions.choice: one band ... one hill: a single close unit on a hilltop
decisions.reason: "One" with "hill" means "a certain hill". Gathered tightly on high ground, the Benjaminites could defend themselves while Abner called out to Joab.

decisions.choice: the Benjaminites; the men from the tribe of Benjamin
decisions.reason: These are fighting men only, so there is no setting for "sons" here.

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אַבְנֵ֜ר אֶל־יוֹאָ֗ב וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ הֲלָנֶ֨צַח֙ תֹּ֣אכַל חֶ֔רֶב הֲל֣וֹא יָדַ֔עְתָּה כִּֽי־מָרָ֥ה תִהְיֶ֖ה בָּאַחֲרוֹנָ֑ה וְעַד־מָתַי֙ לֹֽא־תֹאמַ֣ר לָעָ֔ם לָשׁ֖וּב מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And called Abner to Joab and said, [Is it] forever [that] will devour [the] sword? Not do you know that bitter it will be at the end? And until when not will you say to the people to turn from after their brothers?
pieces: Abner shouted to Joab, "Must the sword go on killing forever? Do you not see that this will end in bitterness? How long before you order the troops to stop chasing their own brothers?"

L.26: And Abner called to Joab and said, "Shall the sword devour forever? Do you not know that it will be bitter at the end? And how long will you not tell the people to turn back from after their brothers?"

R.26: Abner called out to Joab, "Do we have to keep killing each other forever? Surely you know that this will only end in grief. When will you tell your soldiers to stop chasing their own people?"

decisions.choice: the sword devours: killing in war goes on
decisions.reason: The sword is pictured as eating up lives (Deuteronomy 32:42; 2 Samuel 11:25; 18:8).

decisions.choice: bitter at the end: the fighting will leave lasting grief and hatred
decisions.reason: Abner warns that a war between kin, once begun, ends in sorrow for both sides.

decisions.choice: their brothers: fellow Israelites
decisions.reason: Judah and the other tribes are one people, descended from the sons of Jacob. Abner appeals to that bond.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); your soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the soldiers" or "the army".

decisions.choice: their own people
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that "brothers" means fellow Israelites, not only blood brothers.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יוֹאָ֔ב חַ֚י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים כִּ֥י לוּלֵ֖א דִּבַּ֑רְתָּ כִּ֣י אָ֤ז מֵֽהַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ נַעֲלָ֣ה הָעָ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ מֵאַחֲרֵ֥י אָחִֽיו׃
records.gloss: And said Joab, Living [is] God, that if not you had spoken, that then from the morning would have gone up the people, each from after his brother.
pieces: Joab answered, "As surely as God lives, if you had not spoken up, the troops would not have broken off chasing their brothers until the morning."

L.27: And Joab said, "[As] God lives, if you had not spoken, surely then from the morning the people would have gone up, each from after his brother."

R.27: Joab answered, "I swear by the living God: if you had not said this, my soldiers would have kept chasing their own people all night, until morning."

decisions.choice: if you had not spoken, the pursuit would have gone on until morning
alternatives: if you had not spoken (proposing the contest), the troops would have gone home this morning
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and can be read two ways. Taken this way, Joab means that only Abner's appeal has stopped the chase now; otherwise his men would have kept on through the night. Taken the other way, "if you had not spoken" points back to Abner's proposal of the contest (verse 14): if Abner had not started it, the men would have gone home that morning and no one would have died. Literal keeps the Hebrew's openness.

decisions.choice: as God lives: an oath
decisions.reason: The speaker swears by the life of God that what he says is true.

decisions.choice: gone up from after: withdrawn from the pursuit
decisions.reason: To "go up from after" someone is to break off chasing him.

decisions.choice: the troops; my soldiers
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the soldiers" or "the army".

records.source: וַיִּתְקַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיַּֽעַמְדוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וְלֹֽא־יִרְדְּפ֥וּ ע֖וֹד אַחֲרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְלֹֽא־יָסְפ֥וּ ע֖וֹד לְהִלָּחֵֽם׃
records.gloss: And blew Joab on the shofar, and stood still all the people, and not they pursued again after Israel, and not they continued again to fight.
pieces: Joab sounded the trumpet, and the whole army came to a halt. They gave up the chase after Israel, and the fighting ended.

L.28: And Joab blew the trumpet, and all the people stood still; and they did not pursue after Israel any more, and they did not fight any more.

R.28: Then Joab blew the ram's horn. All his soldiers stopped. They did not chase the men of Israel any longer, and there was no more fighting.

decisions.choice: trumpet: a ram's horn, blown as a signal in war
decisions.reason: The shofar was a ram's horn, not a metal trumpet. Its blast called men to battle or, as here, told them to stop (Judges 3:27; 1 Samuel 13:3; 2 Samuel 18:16; 20:22).

decisions.choice: Israel: Abner's army of the northern tribes
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: the whole army; all his soldiers
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the soldiers" or "the army". "The whole army" keeps the word "all".

decisions.choice: the ram's horn
decisions.reason: Readable names the instrument itself.

records.source: וְאַבְנֵ֣ר וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֗יו הָֽלְכוּ֙ בָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה כֹּ֖ל הַלַּ֣יְלָה הַה֑וּא וַיַּעַבְר֣וּ אֶת־הַיַּרְדֵּ֗ן וַיֵּֽלְכוּ֙ כָּל־הַבִּתְר֔וֹן וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מַחֲנָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And Abner and his men went through the Arabah all the night the that, and they crossed the Jordan, and they went all the Bitron, and they came [to] Mahanaim.
pieces: Abner and his men marched all that night through the Arabah. They crossed the Jordan, went on through the whole Bitron, and came to Mahanaim.

L.29: And Abner and his men went through the Arabah all that night, and they crossed the Jordan and went through all the Bitron, and came [to] Mahanaim.

R.29: Abner and his men marched all that night through the Jordan Valley. They crossed the Jordan River, went on through the whole Bitron, and reached Mahanaim.

decisions.choice: the Arabah: the deep valley of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The Arabah is the low, hot rift valley through which the Jordan runs, east of Gibeon.

decisions.choice: the Bitron: probably a ravine or region east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to cut or divide, so it may name a gorge leading up to Mahanaim. It is not found elsewhere. It may instead be a time word, "the whole morning", matching "all that night" earlier in the verse.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: Ish-bosheth's base
decisions.reason: Abner returns to where he had set up Ish-bosheth as king (verse 8).

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley; the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the Arabah" and adds "River".

records.source: וְיוֹאָ֗ב שָׁ֚ב מֵאַחֲרֵ֣י אַבְנֵ֔ר וַיִּקְבֹּ֖ץ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֑ם וַיִּפָּ֨קְד֜וּ מֵעַבְדֵ֥י דָוִ֛ד תִּשְׁעָֽה־עָשָׂ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ וַעֲשָׂה־אֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And Joab returned from after Abner and gathered all the people; and were missing of [the] servants of David nineteen men and Asahel.
pieces: When Joab came back from chasing Abner, he gathered all the troops together. Nineteen of David's men were missing, besides Asahel.

L.30: And Joab returned from following Abner and gathered all the people; and there were missing of the servants of David nineteen men and Asahel.

R.30: Joab stopped chasing Abner and came back. He brought all his soldiers together. Nineteen of David's soldiers were missing, and Asahel too.

decisions.choice: were missing: had been counted and not found, that is, were dead
decisions.reason: The verb is used of men missing when a force is counted after battle (Numbers 31:49; 1 Samuel 20:18).

decisions.choice: and Asahel: named on his own
decisions.reason: Asahel is set apart from the nineteen because he was the commander's brother, and his death will shape what follows (3:27, 30).

decisions.choice: the troops; David's men; his soldiers
decisions.reason: When "the people" means an army in the field, Literal keeps "the people", Balanced says "the troops" and Readable "the soldiers" or "the army". David's "servants" are his fighting men, as in verse 12.

records.source: וְעַבְדֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד הִכּוּ֙ מִבִּנְיָמִ֔ן וּבְאַנְשֵׁ֖י אַבְנֵ֑ר שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵא֧וֹת וְשִׁשִּׁ֛ים אִ֖ישׁ מֵֽתוּ׃
records.gloss: And [the] servants of David had struck of Benjamin and among [the] men of Abner; three hundred and sixty men died.
pieces: But David's men had struck down men of Benjamin and of Abner's forces, and 360 of them died.

L.31: And the servants of David had struck down [men] of Benjamin and among the men of Abner: 360 men died.

R.31: But David's soldiers had killed 360 men from Benjamin and from Abner's army.

decisions.choice: 360 men died: the total of the dead on Abner's side
decisions.reason: The verse joins the men of Benjamin and the rest of Abner's men into one count.

decisions.choice: twenty against 360: a heavy defeat for Abner
decisions.reason: Set beside David's losses (verse 30), the numbers show how one-sided the battle was, and they look ahead to 3:1, where David's house grows stronger while Saul's grows weaker.
Numbers above ninety-nine are written as numerals.

decisions.choice: David's men; David's soldiers
decisions.reason: As in verse 12.

records.source: וַיִּשְׂאוּ֙ אֶת־עֲשָׂהאֵ֔ל וַֽיִּקְבְּרֻ֨הוּ֙ בְּקֶ֣בֶר אָבִ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּ֣ית לָ֑חֶם וַיֵּלְכ֣וּ כָל־הַלַּ֗יְלָה יוֹאָב֙ וַֽאֲנָשָׁ֔יו וַיֵּאֹ֥ר לָהֶ֖ם בְּחֶבְרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And they lifted up Asahel and buried him in [the] tomb of his father, which [is in] Bethlehem. And went all the night Joab and his men, and it became light for them at Hebron.
pieces: They took Asahel and buried him in his father's tomb at Bethlehem. Then Joab and his men marched all night, and day broke as they reached Hebron.

L.32: And they lifted up Asahel and buried him in the tomb of his father, which [was in] Bethlehem. And Joab and his men went all night, and it became light for them at Hebron.

R.32: They carried Asahel's body away to Bethlehem and buried him there in his father's tomb. Joab and his men marched through the whole night. The sun was coming up when they got to Hebron.

decisions.choice: his father's tomb in Bethlehem: the family burial place
decisions.reason: People were buried with their family. Bethlehem was the home town of David's family (1 Samuel 16:1; 17:12), and Asahel's mother Zeruiah was David's sister (1 Chronicles 2:16). The town lay on the way from Gibeon to Hebron.

decisions.choice: it became light for them at Hebron: dawn came as they arrived
decisions.reason: The march from Gibeon to Hebron took the whole night.

decisions.choice: Asahel's body
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that they carried the dead man's body.
